A1 — An IC supply pin operates above its rating or below its minimum operating voltage.
Why it matters: An IC needs a supply inside its operating range.
V0 components: U1/U2 ADS1298; U6 ESP32; U4/U7 LDOs.
V0 finding: ADC AVDD/AVDD1 pins 19/21/22/54/56/59 are on source-free +3.3VA. This confirms missing power under H2, but the floating voltage cannot be assigned a number. DVDD48/50 and U6.2 are on +3.3V relative to AGND.,"CANNOT VERIFY. The missing analog-source connection is corrected under H2: U1/U2 AVDD19/21/22/54/56/59 and DVDD48/50 now reach /+3.3V from U3.1/.2
column2: negatives reach /GND. Nominal 3.3 V meets ADC analog 2.7–5.25 V, digital 1.65–3.6 V and ESP module 3.0–3.6 V ranges. Actual loaded voltage is unmeasured, and the V0 floating voltage was unknown: do not count a numerical undervoltage as FIXED. Keep connections
column3: identify fitted DevKit/source and measure supplies at U3 and both ADCs during startup and Wi-Fi loading. S1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1298.pdf), S2 (https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf)"

Why it matters: Capacitor voltage must remain below its terminal-to-terminal rating.

No value change or added capacitor follows solely from this check. The 5.2 V projection is not a guaranteed overshoot maximum. No excluded tolerance/DC-bias analysis performed. S1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1298.pdf)"

That is a compatibility question, not proof that the present rail oscillates. Do not delete ADC bypasses without evidence. S3 (https://dl.espressif.com/dl/schematics/SCH_ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1_V1.1_20221130.pdf), S4 (https://www.sg-micro.com/rect/assets/54089b71-cc25-4f36-af2e-34b07f00a108/SGM2212.pdf)"

V0 finding: GPIO0/45/46 have defined internal default pulls. GPIO3 has no pull, but its effect depends on eFuse-selected JTAG policy; normal boot failure is unproven.,"CANNOT VERIFY. column2: R34 similarly biases RESET36 and R33 START38. Retain pulls

column4: a pull does not override actively driven warm-reset states. S1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1298.pdf), S2 (https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf)"

Why it matters: Undefined controls can make power/reset/clock selection unpredictable.
V0 components: U4/U7 EN; U1/U2 controls, CLKSEL and DGND straps.
V0 finding: Floating LDO enable, unreferenced DGND strap island, ADC reset/start/enable GPIO nets, and CLK37 tied only to CLKSEL52.,"FIXED. Old floating LDO /EN removed
column2: intended low straps now share real /GND. R33–R37=10 kΩ define START/RESET/PWDN/MOSI/SCLK and R39/R40 define CS high. U1 CLKSEL52=3V3, U2 CLKSEL52=GND
column3: both CLK37 join /ADC_CLK. No missing passive bias/clock connection remains for these V0 omissions. Firmware must enable U1 CLK_EN and validate master-first reset/recovery. Check held-reset defaults and measure clock at both chips. S1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1298.pdf), S2 (https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf)"

column1:
J4 — A controller input exceeds its maximum input voltage.
Why it matters: An MCU input must stay within its local supply-referenced voltage limits.
V0 components: U6 MISO20/DRDY12.
V0 finding: Nominal 3.3 V ADC outputs do not show overvoltage; actual fault-state waveforms absent.,"NOT FOUND. MISO U3.37 and DRDY U3.38/.39 receive ADC outputs on the same 3.3 V rail/ground. No 5 V GPIO connection or excessive static input voltage found in either revision. Board USB5 V is an internal power input, not GPIO drive. No level shifter justified by these connections
column2: startup/overshoot remain measurement checks under E9/L2/I2."

column1:
K1 — A GPIO exceeds its permitted current.
Why it matters: An excessive load or incompatible driven state can overstress a GPIO.
V0 components: U6 ADC-control GPIOs; ADS GPIO pins 42/44/45/46.
V0 finding: No heavy DC GPIO load shown; actual directions, drive and fault-state currents unspecified.,"CANNOT VERIFY. Bias currents are≈0.33 mA when driving against 10 kΩ, with no demonstrated overload. Actual GPIO/ADC modes unknown. Grounded ADS GPIO42/44/45/46 must remain inputs/output-low
column2: optional modes on tied analog pins must stay off. Inspect/read back configuration and restart states. No driver/series resistor justified from a hypothetical misconfiguration."

column1:
K2 — Two output pins drive incompatible levels onto the same net.
Why it matters: Opposing active outputs can contend.
V0 components: U1.43 MISO; U2.43→U1.41.
V0 finding: Daisy path keeps ADC DOUT pins on different nets. No hard two-DOUT short.,"CANNOT VERIFY. U1/U2 DOUT43 share /SPI_MISO with U3 GPIO40. This is supported with separate CS and high-impedance deselected DOUT
column2: R39/R40 default deselection. Actual firmware exclusivity and JTAG/input ownership are unverified. Keep shared bus
column3: configure one CS low at a time and GPIO40–42 as inputs. Scope both CS/MISO during boot/reset/reads and inspect eFuses. ERC output/output alone is not proof of conflict. S1 §9.4.2.1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1298.pdf), S2 (https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf)"

K3 — The controller drives a component whose supply is off.
Why it matters: Driving an unpowered receiver can inject input current.
V0 components: U6→U1/U2.
V0 finding: Analog supply has no source, but digital supply is nominally present; no actual GPIO-high/off-state timing supplied.,"CANNOT VERIFY. Common always-connected MCU/ADC3V3 removes separate carrier power domains. PWDN is an operating control, not a drawn DVDD switch. Actual ramp/reset combinations are unmeasured. Validate actual supply/control timing
column2: do not equate power-down mode with physically removed DVDD or add isolation without a demonstrated state. S1 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1298.pdf)"

column1:
L1 — A state change causes a supply dip or brownout reset.
Why it matters: A load transition can lower the rail and cause brownout, a reset due to low supply.
V0 components: BT1/LDOs/U6.
V0 finding: No state-transition/current/supply waveform or source-impedance model.,"CANNOT VERIFY. Wi-Fi and ADCs share the DevKit rail
column2: actual source/load budget and transition traces remain absent. Capture 3V3 at U3/ADCs, LDO input and reset reason under actual Wi-Fi/ADC changes. No brownout event established
column3: do not add bulk capacitance or a separate rail before measuring. C6’s 5% threshold is 165 mV."

column1:

Why it matters: A GPIO high before receiver power is valid can violate sequencing.
V0 components: U6 controls→ADS1298.
V0 finding: Reset GPIO default levels are not guaranteed; no timing capture proves a high-before-valid event.,CANNOT VERIFY. R33–R37 give low defaults while GPIOs are high impedance
column2: common rails reduce supply differences. CS pulls rise with the rail
column3: precise ramp behavior and warm-reset active states remain unverified. Capture rails/CS/RESET/PWDN/forward GPIOs and validate startup note. Consult TI about CS ramp guidance if unresolved
